components.cost_effect: Uses the same single reward observation; division by the selected probability and state updates are computational costs, not extra Oracle calls.
components.goal: Recover each fixed action reward in conditional expectation from selected-action feedback.
components.key_estimate: E[hat{x}_j(t) | I_1,...,I_{t-1}]=x_j(t); 0<=gamma hat{x}_j(t)/K<=1. Source equations (2) and (11).
components.name: Importance-weighted reward estimator
components.operation: Use hat{x}_j(t)=1{I_t=j}x_j(t)/p_j(t), evaluated only for the observed action; set other entries to zero.
components.requires: p_j(t)>=gamma/K>0 and fixed reward assignment with x_j(t) in [0,1].

limitations.statement: The tuned bound requires a known positive upper bound g for the target horizon. Figure 1 itself supplies no unknown-g tuning or high-probability guarantee.

variants.cost: Exactly one selected-action reward observation and one categorical action draw per trial, hence T of each through T trials. Literal Figure 1 computes K probabilities and traverses K weights per trial; a direct implementation uses O(K) real-arithmetic work and O(K) state, plus exponential evaluation for the nonzero weight update. These operation counts describe the pseudocode, not a source bit-complexity theorem; numerical precision and exponential evaluation costs are separate from feedback calls.
variants.implementation_details_ref: Figure 1, PDF p6 / printed p53; tuning discussion PDF pp6–7
variants.name: Figure 1 Exp3, fixed reward assignment
variants.output: At each trial the played action I_t and its received reward; no terminal best-action recommendation is specified.
public_inputs: Optional positive upper bound g>=Gmax(T), with K>=2, for Corollary 3.2 tuning
variants.query_and_update: At each t compute W_t=sum_j w_j(t) and p_i(t)=(1-gamma)w_i(t)/W_t+gamma/K for every i. Draw I_t from p(t), play I_t and receive x_{I_t}(t). Set hat{x}_{I_t}(t)=x_{I_t}(t)/p_{I_t}(t), and hat{x}_j(t)=0 for j!=I_t. For every j set w_j(t+1)=w_j(t) exp(gamma hat{x}_j(t)/K). Increment t.
variants.requirements: Fixed arbitrary reward assignment x(t) in [0,1]^K. Only the selected action reward is observed. Algorithmic randomization samples the action from the current probability vector.
variants.state_and_initialization: Set w_i(1)=1 for every i in {1,...,K}; maintain positive weights and trial counter t=1.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Figure 1 runs indefinitely with fixed gamma; evaluate or externally stop after any positive integer T. If K>=2 and a positive public g>=Gmax(T) is known, Corollary 3.2 uses gamma=min{1,sqrt(K ln K/((e-1)g))}; g=T is valid for known T. Do not use that displayed tuning formula at K=1 or g=0. Fixed gamma remains well-defined there. No restart or unknown-g adaptation is included.
